He expects way too much even for a design studio. It is impossible to reach his expectations.

It is possible to look at the previous ARCH301 works of his studio, and conclude that every project is disturbingly similar -compared to the other studios-. (Use of spiral staircases, unreasonably long and narrow buildings with accordion doors, etc.) That is a result of Giorgio's behavior. Sometimes he comes to the studio late without acknowledging us. Additionally, I don't believe that he was fair while grading the works. 

In an architectural design studio, I think I begin to forget how to design which I personally believe is the worst thing that can happen.

I cannot see any positive features about the course overall.

First of all, you never feel like you are in charge and you are the designer of this project but rather you are just responsible for preparing visuals and drawings based on his ideas. He is exceptionally directive and does not care what you want or what you like and often humiliates your ideas. I am sure that every person can easily realize that all the projects at the end of the semester are disturbingly similar. But still, these were not important problems compared to the fact that all students started from scratch at the end of each critique session. I draw 7-to 8 different plans which do not have anything in common. He is not familiar with words like "progress" or "process" . Additionally, he acts like all drawings and materials are coming from space without any effort so he has inconceivable expectations. For me as a student, an instructor should understand each student's personal design conception and lead accordingly, however, in this studio students were the ones that are trying to understand his ideas. Design process works if you are making progress by solving problems but in this semester it was an intolerable loop.

Even when we brought different ideas, he ultimately steered them toward the design he had in mind, and most projects ended up looking similar. Additionally, I don’t think he managed the critique schedule well. While some groups received two hours of critique, many didn’t get any at times. Lastly, I couldn’t understand his grading system or what he liked or disliked. In the pin-up, he gave low grades to things he praised as “successful” or “good.”

I feel like my perspective on design didn’t expand this semester.

The positive side is that he does not favor the student like other studio teachers. However, it is not clear what he wants and where he deducts points. You do not get what you deserve. He gives very long critiques but, as an authority figure he should determine his own time management but since he does not set a limit, it causes chaos in the class.
